subject: Agriculture
title: Mutation Breeding
description: A quick win: understand Mutation Breeding.

hook.text: Over 3,000 crop varieties were created by bombarding seeds with radiation. It's not considered GMO.

buildup.text: Starting in the 1950s, scientists exposed seeds to gamma rays or chemicals to randomly shuffle DNA.

discovery.text: Most mutants died or were useless. But rare helpful mutations—shorter stalks, disease resistance—were selected.

twist.text: Ruby Red grapefruit, most modern barley, and many rice varieties came from radiation breeding. You've eaten them.

climax.text: Mutation breeding is unregulated worldwide—even though it randomly scrambles DNA far more than targeted gene editing.

punchline.text: Random radiation: fine. Precise editing: regulated. The logic is backwards.

quiz.question: How many crop varieties have been created through mutation breeding?
